title: The British theologians: preliminary effects can be stifled
source_text: XLVIII. Hi praecedanei effectus, virtute verbi spiritusque in hominum mentibus producti, rebellis voluntatis vitio, suffocari ac penitus extingui possunt, & in multis solent; adeo ut nonnulli in quorum mentibus virtute verbi spiritusque impressa fuit aliqualis notitia veritatis divinae, aliqualis dolor de peccatis suis, aliquod desiderium & aliqua cura liberationis, mutentur plane in contrarium, veritatem rejiciant & odio habeant, concupiscentiis suis se tradant, in peccatis occalleant, & absque desiderio vel cura liberationis in iisdem computrescant.
pass_a_gloss: XLVIII. These preceding effects, produced in the minds of men by the power of the word and spirit, can be suffocated and wholly extinguished by the vice of the rebellious will, & in many are wont to be; so that some in whose minds by the power of the word and spirit was impressed some knowledge of divine truth, some sorrow for their sins, some desire & some care of deliverance, are changed plainly into the contrary, reject the truth & hold it in hatred, give themselves up to their lusts, grow callous in sins, & without desire or care of deliverance rot away in them.
pass_b_english: Thesis XLVIII. 'These preliminary effects, produced in people's minds by the power of the word and Spirit, can be smothered and entirely put out through the fault of a rebellious will, and in many they usually are.

So some people, in whose minds the power of the word and Spirit has stamped a measure of knowledge of divine truth, some grief for their sins, and some longing and concern for deliverance, are turned completely the other way: they reject the truth and hate it, hand themselves over to their desires, grow hardened in their sins, and rot in them with no longing or concern for deliverance.'
